request.project_task: Build an online symptom triage and appointment routing service.
request.project_goal: Route non-emergency requests while identifying cases needing urgent help.
request.project_description: A patient answers questions; the service gives a routing recommendation and schedules eligible requests.

functional_requirements.text: A patient selects a symptom category.

atoms.text: A patient selects a symptom category.

functional_requirements.text: The system displays an emergency warning when configured red flags are present.

atoms.text: The system displays an emergency warning when configured red flags are present.

functional_requirements.text: The system recommends a care route for non-emergency answers.

atoms.text: The system recommends a care route for non-emergency answers.

functional_requirements.text: The patient books an offered appointment.

atoms.text: The patient books an offered appointment.

functional_requirements.text: A clinician reviews submitted answers before the appointment.

atoms.text: A clinician reviews submitted answers before the appointment.

functional_requirements.text: The patient can correct answers before clinician review.

The requirements do not provide the red-flag rule set.
Sensitive answers must be accessible only to the patient and assigned clinician.

use_cases.name: Complete Symptom Triage
use_cases.goal: Allow a patient to select a symptom category, answer category-specific questions, and receive an emergency warning or a care route recommendation.
use_cases.trigger: Patient starts a non-emergency symptom triage request.

preconditions.text: The patient has access to the Triage Route service.

success_postconditions.text: The patient has received a care route recommendation for non-emergency answers.

failure_postconditions.text: The patient has received an emergency warning because configured red flags were present.

main_success_scenario.name: Non-emergency triage and care route recommendation

steps.action: The patient selects a symptom category.
The system evaluates the answers for configured red flags.
steps.expected_result: No configured red flags are present.

steps.action: The system recommends a care route for the non-emergency answers.
steps.expected_result: A care route recommendation is displayed to the patient.

alternative_scenarios.name: Patient corrects answers before clinician review

steps.action: The patient chooses to correct previously submitted answers before clinician review.
steps.expected_result: The patient can edit the answers.

steps.action: The patient submits the corrected answers.

exception_scenarios.name: Emergency warning due to red flags

steps.action: The system detects configured red flags in the patient's answers.

system_stories.responsibility: Detect emergency indicators and display an emergency warning when present.

system_stories.system_action: Generate a care route recommendation for non-emergency answers.

system_stories.responsibility: Permit the patient to update answers prior to clinician review.

use_cases.name: Book Offered Appointment
use_cases.goal: Allow a patient to book an appointment offered after a non-emergency care route recommendation.
use_cases.trigger: The patient receives a care route recommendation and an appointment is offered.

preconditions.text: The patient has completed triage and received a non-emergency care route recommendation.

success_postconditions.text: The patient has booked an offered appointment.

steps.action: The system offers an appointment based on the care route recommendation.
steps.expected_result: An appointment option is presented to the patient.

steps.action: The patient books the offered appointment.

user_stories.benefit: I can secure a time to receive care.

system_stories.system_action: Offer an appointment based on the care route recommendation.
system_stories.responsibility: Present available appointment options to the patient.

use_cases.human_readable_text: After receiving a non-emergency care route recommendation, the patient books an offered appointment.

use_cases.goal: Allow a clinician to review a patient's submitted answers before the appointment.
use_cases.trigger: A patient has submitted answers and an appointment is scheduled.

preconditions.text: The patient has submitted answers and an appointment is scheduled.

success_postconditions.text: The clinician has reviewed the submitted answers before the appointment.

failure_postconditions.text: The clinician cannot access or review the submitted answers.

steps.action: The clinician accesses the patient's submitted answers before the appointment.
steps.expected_result: The submitted answers are displayed to the clinician.

steps.action: The clinician reviews the submitted answers.
steps.expected_result: The clinician has reviewed the answers.

user_stories.capability: review submitted answers before the appointment

issues.message: Edge ADE-UC001-001 must link to UC step(s) or be marked unsupported
Edge ADE-UC001-008 must link to UC step(s) or be marked unsupported

The alternative scenario 'Patient corrects answers before clinician review' is modeled as a decision immediately after answering questions, before red-flag evaluation. This is a reasonable equivalent decomposition of the UC's alternative flow and does not contradict any supplied step, but the placement of the correction branch before evaluation is a modeling choice rather than an explicit UC ordering.

details.summary: The activity diagram preserves all main, alternative, and exception steps of UC-001. The correction alternative is represented as a decision branch, the red-flag evaluation and emergency warning exception are present, and the non-emergency care route recommendation is modeled. No unsupported business actions or omitted UC steps were found; the only observation is a non-blocking modeling choice regarding the placement of the correction branch.

issues.message: Edge ADE-UC003-001 must link to UC step(s) or be marked unsupported
Edge ADE-UC003-005 must link to UC step(s) or be marked unsupported

The decision node 'Are the submitted answers accessible?' and the failure final node 'Answers not accessible' introduce an accessibility branch that is not present in the UC's main, alternative, or exception scenarios. The UC defines a failure postcondition but no exception scenario or step describing this branch, so this is a non-blocking semantic warning rather than a step-level omission or contradiction.

The 'System displays the submitted answers to the clinician' action is placed in the 'Triage Route Service' partition (ACT-003), but the UC's expected result for STEP-UC003-001 is a system display behavior not explicitly assigned to the secondary actor. This is a traceability observation only and does not contradict any UC step.

details.summary: The activity diagram preserves both main success steps (access and review of submitted answers) and the success postcondition. The added accessibility decision and failure final node are not explicitly grounded in a UC exception scenario, but they align with the UC's failure postcondition and do not omit or contradict any supplied step. No evidence-grounded blocking issue remains, so the diagram is accepted with non-blocking warnings.

issues.message: Step STEP-UC002-001 references FRs outside UC-002: FR-004

FR-003 emergency warning is modeled as a failure postcondition (POST-UC001-002) and exception scenario (SCN-UC001-EXC-001) rather than a success outcome; this is a modeling preference, not a direct FR contradiction, since the warning is still represented.

UC-002 STEP-UC002-001 cites FR-004 as the source for offering an appointment, but FR-004 only covers recommending a care route; the appointment offering is an inferred step. This is a traceability nuance, not a blocking omission.
